clue.text: Comprehensive collection of books in vehicle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a single volume gathering several works together
second meaning: the full old name for a bus

explanation.surface: A complete set of books being carted around in a van.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests books stored in a vehicle; 'in' merely joins two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a bound anthology of several novels and the horse-drawn or motor public carriage later shortened to bus.

clue.text: Eye-care: book test after work

indicators.note: 'after' places the first two pieces behind the third in the finished word

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a piece of work
a tome is a large book
to try is to test

explanation.surface: An eye examination in which you read from a book once your job is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Optometry is the profession of examining eyesight and prescribing lenses, a field of eye health.

clue.text: Man on board heard in the dark

indicators.note: 'heard' means we want a word that is spoken the same as the chess piece

parts.note: a chess piece, a 'man' on the chessboard

explanation.surface: A sailor on deck is heard calling out in darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a ship, but the board is a chessboard and the man a knight, which loses its silent K when said.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the period of darkness between sunset and dawn, so 'the dark' is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Pointed remark, suggestion involving English roast

indicators.note: 'involving' says the two clue pieces hold something between them

parts.note: a barb is a cutting comment
E is the abbreviation for English
a cue is a hint or prompt

explanation.surface: A sharp comment and a hint about the English way of roasting meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The remark and the suggestion together enclose the single letter for English, which sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To barbecue is to cook meat over an open fire, a way of roasting it, and the word also names the outdoor meal.

clue.text: Dish on plate — items she used

indicators.note: 'used' suggests something worn or knocked about, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A meal served up on a plate, made with whatever she used.
explanation.walkthrough: A Spanish omelette is a thick egg-and-potato tortilla.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish omelette is a cooked egg and potato preparation served as a meal, an example of a dish.

clue.text: Humbles me after interrupting church dignitaries

indicators.note: 'interrupting' tells us one piece cuts into the middle of the other

parts.note: deans are senior clergy in a cathedral
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone humiliated after butting in on a meeting of senior churchmen.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower their dignity, so it is a verb synonym for humbling them.

clue.text: Western film jaundiced — hang on, that's wrong

indicators.note: 'that's wrong' says the letters as given are in the wrong arrangement and must be put right

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cynical critic interrupting to say a cowboy movie got something wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Django Unchained is Quentin Tarantino's 2012 film, set in the American South and West.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarantino's film is styled as a spaghetti-style cowboy picture, so it is a fair example of a Western.

clue.text: Elephant keeper, married, with a husband no longer in the game

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for married
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband
a player who is out has been eliminated

explanation.surface: A zookeeper's marriage, the husband having dropped out of the running.
explanation.definitionFit: A mahout is the person in India or South-East Asia who drives and tends a working elephant.

clue.text: Nocturnal creature in a stream grabbing Daffy Duck?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to grab something is to take hold of it, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a rill is a small brook
daffy is informal for crazy
a duck is a zero score in cricket, the shape of O

explanation.surface: Some animal of the night in a brook catching the cartoon character Daffy Duck.
explanation.walkthrough: Daffy Duck looks like one name, but 'Daffy' gives one piece and 'Duck' another; the brook holds the first, and the second follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo, an armoured mammal of the Americas, mostly forages after dark, making it a creature of the night.

clue.text: Impertinent answer covering Saints

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap around it, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: to say is to answer or reply
S is the abbreviation for saint, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A cheeky reply that glosses over the saints.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassy is informal for cheeky or disrespectful, an adjective synonym for impertinent.

clue.text: Row about good, formidable opponent

indicators.note: 'about' means going around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: An argument about something good turns into a tough contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel; here it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger is a figurative term for a fierce, aggressive competitor, someone very hard to beat.

clue.text: Three articles, mother's objects of loathing

parts.note: the indefinite articles an and a, then the definite article the
ma is mother, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: Three things belonging to mother that she cannot stand.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is something or someone intensely detested, so the plural fits things that are hated.

clue.text: Astounding rhyme adapted for part of Lent

indicators.note: something adapted has been altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A remarkable verse reworked for use during the Lenten season.
explanation.walkthrough: Mothering Sunday is the British Mother's Day, held on the fourth Sunday of Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: The day falls within the forty days before Easter, so it is one portion of that fasting season.

clue.text: Continuously on strike, everywhere

parts.note: as in working right through, without a break
striking workers are said to be out

explanation.surface: Workers on a continuous strike all over the place.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout as an adverb means in every part, as in a house painted throughout, which matches everywhere.

clue.text: Would-be poet met, merry with sherry

indicators.note: someone merry is tipsy, and tipsy letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An aspiring poet, met at a party, a little tipsy on sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merry' sits between the two words it scrambles, and 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymester is a writer of trivial or poor verse, someone with pretensions to being a real poet.

clue.text: Appeal of Steeple Ashton

indicators.note: 'of' says the answer is drawn out of the words that follow, as part of them

parts.note: found across the two words, at the end of the first and start of the second

explanation.surface: A fundraising appeal from Steeple Ashton, a Wiltshire village.
explanation.walkthrough: Steeple Ashton is a real village in Wiltshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an earnest request, the same as an appeal for help.

clue.text: Footwear item in joint, very British, held up

parts.note: the ankle is a joint of the leg

indicators.note: in a down clue, something held up is raised, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: too means very, as in not too bad
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A shoe caught on a joint, very British, has delayed things.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the second and third pieces are raised; the joint stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: An ankle boot is a shoe reaching just above the ankle, one kind of thing worn on the feet.

clue.text: Gets rid of bad lots

parts.note: food that is bad has gone off
loads means lots, a large amount

explanation.surface: A trader disposes of the poor auction lots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' looks like items for auction; it is simply a large quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: To offload is to unload or dispose of something unwanted, the same as discarding it.

clue.text: Ma's toy?

parts.note: surface reading: a plaything belonging to mother
setter's reading: Ma is the famous cellist, and his first name is also a spinning toy on a string

explanation.walkthrough: The cellist Yo-Yo Ma shares his given name with the toy that climbs and falls on a string, so the toy is, in a sense, his.
explanation.definitionFit: The toy is a disc wound on a string that runs down and back up, and it is also the first name of the cellist.

clue.text: Agricultural worker's garment made by 13?

parts.note: surface reading: an old farm labourer's loose overgarment
setter's reading: the answer to 13 is a verse-maker, and this garment's two halves chime with each other

explanation.walkthrough: The reference is to 13 Down, a writer of verse: the two halves of this compound end with the same sound, as if a versifier had made it.
explanation.definitionFit: A smock frock is the loose, gathered linen overshirt traditionally worn by English farm labourers.

clue.text: Vulgar general

definitions.meaning: second meaning: shared by all, widespread

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like a description of a rude army officer, but each is a separate meaning of one adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective can mean low-class and unrefined, or widely shared, as in common knowledge.

clue.text: A huge amount free, in society as a whole?

parts.note: as in 'it means the world to me'
an escaped prisoner at large is free

explanation.surface: A vast sum released into the community.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the general public or everyone outside one's own circle, matching the whole of society.

clue.text: Quality paintings put up, Italian

indicators.note: in a down clue, something put up is raised, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: paintings collectively are art
IT is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: Fine Italian paintings hung on a gallery wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' looks like hanging pictures; in a down clue it turns the word over.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing characteristic of a person, a synonym for quality in that sense.

clue.text: Breed fish, reportedly

indicators.note: 'reportedly' means as it is spoken, so we want a word with the same sound

parts.note: rays are flat sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone said to be farming fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise animals is to rear them, the same verb as to breed them.

clue.text: Car worker admits to making robot

parts.note: auto is short for automobile

indicators.note: to admit someone is to let them in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a man is a worker, as in manpower
taken as written

explanation.surface: A car-factory employee confesses to building a robot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admits to' reads as confessing; 'admits' is the container signal and 'to' is a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a self-operating machine that moves by itself, which is essentially what a robot is.

clue.text: I turn to follow a male friend

indicators.note: 'to follow' puts the first pieces after the later ones in the finished word

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for male
taken as written
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: I take my turn after a man, as a pal would.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend and is used informally in English for a pal.

clue.text: Recent plays by key dramatist

indicators.note: to play with something is to move it about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: New stage works by an important playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plays' and 'dramatist' sit naturally together, hiding that 'plays' is the anagram signal; Terence was a Roman comic playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence, the second-century BC Roman, wrote six surviving comedies, making him a classical playwright.

clue.text: Sweet, having hair swept back

indicators.note: something swept back is pushed the other way, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: tresses are locks of hair, so tressed means having hair

explanation.surface: A pretty person with hair swept back off the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective for a charming person; here it is the British word for a pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a sweet is the pudding course of a meal, which is what a dessert is.
